clue.text: Weekend drinks container with rings round it

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase standing for the ringed planet

parts.note: SAT is short for Saturday, one day of the weekend
an urn holds tea or coffee for serving

explanation.surface: A big tea urn is set out for the weekend with rings stacked around it.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a description, not a synonym: the sixth planet is famous for its rings.
explanation.definitionFit: The sixth planet from the Sun is the one best known for its wide encircling ring system.

clue.text: Previously for a considerable period

explanation.surface: Something happened earlier and lasted a long while.
explanation.definitionFit: As one word it means former or at one time; split as two words it means a fairly long stretch.

clue.text: Sent a message to Terry, former editor

parts.note: Tel is a familiar British short form of the name Terry
ex means one-time or former

explanation.surface: A note was dispatched to Terry, who used to edit the paper.
explanation.walkthrough: Tel as a pet form of Terry is a British nickname habit.
explanation.definitionFit: To transmit a message by the old teleprinter network was to use that verb.

clue.text: Having a slowing effect on arrant Ted-remarkably

indicators.note: doing something remarkably suggests an unusual reshaping, so the letters of the words before it are rearranged

explanation.surface: Ted, an arrant slowcoach, has a remarkable knack of holding things up.
explanation.definitionFit: A substance that slows a process, such as fire spread, is so called.

clue.text: I lost a switch, gold switch

indicators.note: to switch things is to swap them around, so the letters of the preceding words change places

parts.note: OR is the heraldic word for gold

explanation.surface: Someone loses a switch and replaces it with a golden one.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'switch' is the anagram signal on I LOST A, giving ISOLAT; the second is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An electrical device that cuts a circuit off from its supply is a kind of switch.

clue.text: Sack the man given a job in despatch

definitions.text: the man given a job in despatch

explanation.surface: A worker is fired from the dispatch department.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is cryptic: put a man on the packing line in despatch and you have done just what the phrase says.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means dismiss someone abruptly, and read literally it describes assigning a fellow to the packing work of a dispatch room.

clue.text: Drink consumed by village revellers

indicators.note: the letters are swallowed up inside the run of the two words that follow

explanation.surface: Beer is downed by the merrymakers of the village.
explanation.definitionFit: A light bottom-fermented beer is a common drink.

clue.text: A Frenchman entering different point gets a plug

indicators.note: going into shows one piece placed inside another
made different, the letters of the word point are rearranged

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur, a Frenchman's title

explanation.surface: A Frenchman going to a different spot obtains a stopper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns POINT into TPION, and 'entering' puts A and M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the wooden stopper fitted into a cannon's muzzle.

clue.text: Let Ray get involved with property in land

indicators.note: getting involved suggests the letters becoming tangled into a new order

explanation.surface: Ray is allowed to dabble in real estate.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the American word for real estate: land and buildings held as property.

clue.text: How one hurried and produced a security device for the door perhaps?

definitions.text: produced a security device for the door perhaps?

explanation.surface: Someone dashed off, or else a locksmith made a fastening.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means ran off fast, and literally it says one manufactured a sliding bar for securing a door.

clue.text: Obstinately slow line of traffic?

parts.note: pictures a convoy of famously stubborn pack animals plodding along in single file

explanation.surface: A frustratingly sluggish queue of vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: A string of mules carrying goods is a procession of beasts known for stubbornness.

clue.text: Ray's a character in Greece

explanation.surface: A man named Ray is a notable figure on a Greek island.
explanation.definitionFit: It names a kind of high-energy radiation and the third Greek letter.

clue.text: There is no duty on model tool, no cost either

parts.note: the Model T was the famous early Ford car, so model gives T
ax is the American spelling of axe, a chopping tool
free means costing nothing

explanation.surface: A model tool is offered with nothing to pay and no customs charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Goods exempt from levy carry no excise or customs charge.

clue.text: Plucky instrumentalist?

parts.note: plucky looks like brave, but here means given to plucking strings

explanation.surface: A courageous musician.
explanation.definitionFit: A player of the large stringed instrument plucks its strings.

clue.text: Agencies that inform me returning assistance

indicators.note: something returning comes back the other way, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: aid means help or assistance

explanation.surface: News bodies send help back to me.
explanation.definitionFit: Press, broadcasting and similar channels are the means by which the public is kept informed.

clue.text: Being about to get the lot back it's stupefying

indicators.note: one word placed around another, so the first wraps the reversed piece
coming back means read in the opposite direction

parts.note: a sum is the total, the whole lot

explanation.surface: Being about to win everything back is overwhelming.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Being' reads as an ordinary opening word but is the container itself; 'the lot' as a total is the trick, and 'it's' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Bewildering or puzzling someone leaves them stupefied.

clue.text: Post Office

explanation.surface: Looks like the name of the national mail service.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words can mean a job or appointment someone holds.

clue.text: Fell in a rush, having done some reorganising

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: a rush is a reed-like marsh plant
Shap Fell is a high moorland pass in Cumbria, northern England

explanation.surface: Someone tumbled hurriedly after a bout of tidying.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fell' looks like a verb but names Shap Fell, a Cumbrian upland; SHAP goes into REED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that has been given a new form or structure has been reorganised.

clue.text: Ships I'll float round

indicators.note: turned round suggests the letters are spun into a fresh order

explanation.surface: Boats bob about as I float in circles.
explanation.definitionFit: A small fleet of vessels is so called.

clue.text: Ornament of open fabric in a musical instrument

indicators.note: one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: a lute is a plucked stringed instrument
net is an open-mesh fabric

explanation.surface: A lacy decoration sits inside an instrument case.
explanation.definitionFit: A crescent-shaped decorative panel or window in architecture or design is so called.

clue.text: Right of ownership a peer has

explanation.surface: A nobleman holds the deeds to his estate.
explanation.definitionFit: It means legal ownership of property, and also the rank-name such as Earl or Duke that a member of the nobility holds.

clue.text: One is pressed to make a report

definitions.text: One is pressed to make a report

parts.words: One is pressed to make a report
parts.note: a report here is a bang, the noise a gun makes when the firing lever is squeezed

explanation.surface: Someone is urged to file an account.
explanation.definitionFit: Squeezing a gun's firing lever produces the loud bang called a report.

clue.text: A maths problem could leave on breathless

indicators.note: a problem version of the words is a jumbled one, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tough sum leaves a student gasping.
explanation.definitionFit: A respiratory condition that constricts the airways can leave a sufferer gasping for air.

clue.text: Order a player to take no further part tin the going-away party

definitions.text: Order a player to take no further part

explanation.surface: A referee dismisses a player during a farewell gathering.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb phrase it means dismiss from the field, and as a noun it means a farewell celebration.

clue.text: Drunk when taken from well!

parts.note: drunk means tipsy, and also a lubricant pumped from a well has been put on something

explanation.surface: Water from a well is drunk.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for tipsy, and literally greased with what is drawn from a well.

clue.text: Rascally Kelvin, his van crashed

parts.note: K is the symbol for the kelvin, a unit of temperature

indicators.note: a crashed van is wrecked, so the letters of the words before are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A roguish Kelvin wrecked his van.
explanation.definitionFit: Dishonest and roguish behaviour is that of a scoundrel.

clue.text: Very warm is the Mexican hostelry.

parts.note: hot means very warm
el is the Spanish word for the, as used in Mexico

explanation.surface: A Mexican inn is very warm.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are establishments offering lodging to travellers.

clue.text: Coming second in the hill race?

explanation.surface: A runner is placed second in a fell race.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means finishing as runner-up, and literally describes a racer ascending the slope.

clue.text: One acted out the story

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are thrown out of order and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone performed the tale.
explanation.definitionFit: A short amusing tale about a real incident is a kind of story.

clue.text: Girl burning electricity

parts.note: a fire that is in is still alight
the grid is the network delivering electricity

explanation.surface: A young woman is using up power.
explanation.definitionFit: A girl's given name, famously borne by the actress Bergman.
